title: Planck and horizon dimensional scalings
description: Algebraic combinations of the reduced Planck constant, the speed of light, Newton's gravitational constant and a positive horizon radius. Their dimensions follow from SI units; the expressions alone do not establish corresponding physical observables or laws.
definitions: hbar = h/(2 pi) is the reduced Planck constant.
c is the speed of light in vacuum.
r_s is a positive length; identifying it as a Schwarzschild radius requires the Schwarzschild spacetime assumptions.
assumptions: SI dimensions are used: [hbar] = kg m^2 s^-1, [c] = m s^-1, [G] = m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 and [r_s] = m.
K_skeleton and sigma are names assigned to the stated algebraic combinations, not independently established material properties.
The factor 16 pi is part of the specified definition of sigma; no horizon stress law is inferred from dimensional consistency alone.
mechanism: Substitution of the SI dimensions of hbar, c, G and r_s gives the displayed dimensions. The expressions are algebraic scalings; a separate physical derivation is required to interpret them as observables.
primary_sources: 2019 SI definitions of h and c
CODATA recommended value and unit for Newton's gravitational constant G
Standard definition of reduced Planck constant hbar = h/(2 pi)
falsification_conditions: Recalculation from the stated SI dimensions fails to produce the displayed units.
An interpretation as a physical observable is asserted without an explicit physical definition and derivation.
confusion_guard: Dimensional consistency is necessary but does not establish a physical law. In particular, sigma is not asserted here to be a measured horizon surface tension.
